newsitem.title: GERMANY: EU grain prices seen coming under pressure in 97/98.
newsitem.headline: EU grain prices seen coming under pressure in 97/98.

text.p: An ample European Union 1997 grain crop and stocks additions carried over from 1996 will pressure 1997/98 prices, the Hamburg grain and feeds trade association's grains sector said.
This would be in line with worldwide grain area expansions and slower growth in import markets such as China, it said in a statement.
These developments may lead to export competition and new transatlantic feuds over subsidies, albeit at a more moderate pace than in the late 1980s and early 90s.
The statement said this year's EU grain crop may rise by four percent over 1996 to 205-210 million tonnes because of smaller set-aside and because growth prospects are favourable.
Unsubsidised EU grain exports in 97/98 could roughly total 30 million tonnes after an estimated 25-26 million in 96/97 and 18 million in 95/96.
The total in 96/97 included wheat exports at 10-11 million (6.5 million previously), flour at five million (4.2), barley unchanged at five to six million, and others.

Intervention stocks additions may be five or six million tonnes in the 96/97 season, with the carry-in level at 2.8 million at the beginning of the campaign. --Vera Eckert, Hamburg newsroom, +49-40-41903275
